chapter: Glaser, the Arcadia and bands of 1939-41
title: Golden Gate Ballroom and the pay dispute
summary: At the Golden Gate with five bands, Roy waited for his pay in change.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So we went out of there, made it to... After being on the air. And we came back to New York, we were off for a little while, and then we went to the Arcadia again. But we only stayed four months this time.

In the meantime, the guys... The Golden Gate had just opened up, and they got five bands up there. You know, Coleman was up there, Teddy was up there with his band, Jay McShann had a band, let me see, who else was up there... Let me see, Jay McShann... Leonard...

Harlan Leonard, yeah. Let me see, Jay McShann, Harlan Leonard, Teddy Wilson, Coleman Hawkins, and there was another band, I can't think who it was. So I got the gig up there. I didn't want to go there now, remember, because I just felt like with all those bands, I figure there's gonna be some shit about the money. Heh-heh. And sure enough, it come time to get paid, the cat said, 'Oh, we

don't pay off tonight." I said, "Yeah, but this is the end of my week. I'm supposed to get paid tonight." Well, Coleman was across the street drinking, and I don't know where the rest of the cats were. So I waited. I refused to leave there until I got my money. You know, this cat went around to all the vendors, and I had my trumpet case, I could hardly carry it, loaded with change...!
So behind that, I think we broke the band up. Then I went into Kelly's.
